newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-MAJOLI UPSETS HUBER AT CHASE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MAJOLI UPSETS HUBER AT CHASE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Iva Majoli won her first match at the season-ending Chase Championships in three tries by upseting sixth-seeded Anke Huber 7-5 6-3 on Monday.
Majoli outhit last year's runner-up from the baseline, committing 15 fewer unforced errors in the one hour and 20 minute victory at Madison Square Garden.

"I tried to concentrate hard and tried to win this first match and it wasn't easy. You get a little bit tight when you start thinking, 'oh I can win it for the first time,'" said the 19-year-old Croatian. "But, I handled it pretty good and I won."

Huber got off to a struggling start, making four double faults in her first two service games, and never found the form that had carried the German to the Australian Open final and three singles titles this year.
"I just didn't feel comfortable on the court the whole match," said Huber, 21. "It was just bad."
Ailing defending champion Steffi Graf is scheduled to play her first match in the $2 million tournament against Karina Habsudova of Slovakia Tuesday.
The top-seeded German was forced to quit in the middle of her match against Jana Novotna in the final of the Advanta Championships on Sunday in Philadelphia with a flare-up of chronic back pain.

"She hit for about 20 minutes today and continues to get better," tournament spokesperson Jim Fuhse said of the reigning French, Wimbledon and U.S. Open champion. "Hopefully she will be totally ready for tommorow's match."
Also scheduled for Tuesday is number two-seeded Monica Seles against Japan's Kimiko Date, who is retiring after this tournament.

A first-round loser the last two years in this elite 16-player event, Majoli came out firing, taking a 5-2 first set lead. But Huber, mounted a comeback, winning the next three games, saving a set point on her serve in the 10th game in the process. Two games later, though, Huber dropped a forehand into the net on the second set point to close out the 44-minute set.

Majoli again took a commanding lead in the second set, taking a 3-0 lead with the loss of just six points. She went up 5-1 before Huber again rallied briefly, breaking Majoli's serve in the seventh game and holding serve to make it 5-3.
"I didn't really believe that I could win the match because I just didn't play as well as I should have to win it," Huber said. "It was just gone."
Majoli wrapped up the win on her first match point with a service winner.
